syllabus.quote: Discuss write about issue(s) or topic(s) in depth in a structured way

one_line: Write paragraphs that give benefits and drawbacks of the thing in the question. Expand each point with its reason or effect.

points.heading: Open briefly, then expand each point
points.text: Some mark schemes give marks for a short definition or description of the thing in the question. 18 of the 77 Discuss mark schemes do this. Most allow one mark. June 2025 Paper 31 Q7 allows two. Write one clear opening sentence and move on.

cites.quote: Max one for: • Definition of computer simulation (1)
Max TWO marks:

points.heading: Open briefly, then expand each point
points.text: Marks come from a list of points in the mark scheme. Many points earn a second mark when you expand them with a reason or an effect. The mark scheme shows the point as (1st) and the expansion as (1).

cites.quote: Direct data source/direct data is reliable/trusted (1st) – because we collected it (1)
Must have expansions or comparisons to be a proper discussion

points.heading: Open briefly, then expand each point
points.text: Do not make a point and stop. The March 2022 examiner report says most answers made valid points, but few expanded them. Two November 2022 mark schemes cap answers with no expansion at 6 of 8.

cites.quote: Most responses gained credit for making valid points, but few went on to discuss the points they made by expanding on them.
Max six marks if no attempt at expansion

points.heading: Open briefly, then expand each point
points.text: No Discuss mark scheme from 2022 to 2025 gives a mark for a conclusion or for your opinion. The syllabus meaning of Discuss does not ask for one. The November 2019 examiner report used older wording. It said Discuss often needs a conclusion. A one-line conclusion does no harm. Spend your time on expanded points.

cites.quote: Discuss write about issue(s) or topic(s) in depth in a structured way
Discuss questions require candidates to give the important arguments for and against, and often require a conclusion

points.heading: Cover both sides
points.text: Each side often has its own maximum. 38 of the 77 Discuss mark schemes print a MAX for one side or for each side. On 8-mark questions it is usually 6, sometimes 5 and once 7. On those questions, an answer with only benefits cannot get full marks.

cites.quote: Benefits max 6
Disadvantages MAX five from

points.heading: Cover both sides
points.text: 23 mark schemes, all from 2022 and 2023, need both sides for full marks. 20 of them ask for at least two points on each side. The other 3 are 4-mark and 6-mark questions, and one of each is enough. 4 more mark schemes from November 2023 cap an answer with only benefits or only drawbacks. The June 2025 examiner report says the same.

cites.quote: Must have at least two of each to gain full marks
answers that address only benefits or only drawbacks cannot achieve full marks

points.heading: Cover both sides
points.text: Do not write the same point twice, once as a benefit and again reversed as a drawback. The examiner gives the mark only once, and you lose time.

cites.quote: repeated the list, but in reverse structure, so the positive aspects of one became the negative points of the other
(Converse answer may also be given as an advantage – Award ONCE only)

points.heading: Write in paragraphs
points.text: Bullet points lose marks. Every 2022 and 2023 Discuss mark scheme caps a bulleted list. So do 6 of the 17 from 2024. That makes 48 of the 77. The cap is 6 of 8, 4 or 5 of 6, or 3 of 4.

cites.quote: Max. six marks if bullets/list of points
Max. three marks if bullets/list of points

points.heading: Write in paragraphs
points.text: The 2025 mark schemes do not print the bullet cap. The 2025 examiner reports still say that bulleted lists and tables of statements cannot reach most of the marks. Two separate lists of single words or very short sentences have the same problem.

cites.quote: learners who produced bulleted lists or tables of statements were unable to access most of the marks
answers that have separate lists of benefits and drawbacks, but the lists consist of single word or very brief sentences

points.heading: Write in paragraphs
points.text: Write one paragraph of benefits and one of drawbacks. Put the reason or effect of each point in the same sentence as the point.

cites.quote: Candidates should be encouraged to write answers in full sentences.
The strongest answers were written in full prose style and included points which were expanded upon

points.heading: Name the cost and the people
points.text: Say what the money pays for. The examiners treat 'expensive' or 'costs more' as too vague. Name the spending, for example travel to interviews or printing questionnaires.

cites.quote: Where candidates stated that collecting direct data was expensive, this was considered too vague, but if candidates identified an area on which money would have to be spent, which would not otherwise be spent, this was awarded
Many responses mentioned costs without going into sufficient detail to merit credit.

points.heading: Name the cost and the people
points.text: Link each benefit and drawback to the people or organisation in the question. Answers that described types of technology or the stages of a process got little or no credit. So did answers about the wrong topic.

cites.quote: Descriptions of different types of TEL, statements about benefits or drawbacks gained little or no credit without further comment on how these can affect the achievement of students.
describing the stages of the data mining process or confusing data mining with another topic altogether

question.quote: Data can be collected by using a direct or an indirect data source. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using direct data compared to indirect data.

strong.sentence: The person who will use direct data collects it first-hand (a primary source). Someone else collected indirect data for another purpose (a secondary source).

earns.quote: Simple statement of the difference between the two (1): e.g.

strong.sentence: One advantage of direct data is that it is more reliable and trusted, because the user collected it and knows exactly how.

earns.quote: Direct data source/direct data is reliable/trusted (1st) – because we collected it (1)

strong.sentence: Also, the user collects only specific, relevant data, so no time goes on sorting through data they do not need.
Direct data is also more up to date than indirect data, which someone may have collected years ago.

earns.quote: Direct data is (more) up-to-date (1) Disadvantages MAX SIX

strong.sentence: However, a disadvantage is that the sample size may be small, whereas indirect data sources tend to be much larger sets of data.

earns.quote: The sample size may be small (1st) – whereas indirect data sources tend to be larger sets of data (1)

strong.sentence: Collecting direct data also costs money that would not otherwise be spent, such as travel to interviews and printing questionnaires.

earns.quote: Collecting direct data involves the expense of travelling/photocopying/printing questionnaires//any expense to do with a direct data method (1)

weak.answer: Advantages: direct data is cheaper, relevant, up to date. Disadvantages: indirect data is not relevant and old, direct data is expensive.
weak.why: It is a list of single words. 'Expensive' does not say what the money pays for. The disadvantages repeat the advantages in reverse, so they earn nothing new.

basis.quote: Some candidates effectively wrote what was good about direct data compared to indirect data and then repeated the list, but in reverse structure, so the positive aspects of one became the negative points of the other.

examples.note: The examiner report says this question was about direct data, with indirect data only as a reference point.

question.quote: Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of using data mining in businesses.

strong.sentence: Data mining is the use of software tools to analyse very large data sets.

earns.quote: data mining (is a set of techniques and tools) used to from work on / analyse large data sets

strong.sentence: Its aim is to discover trends, patterns and relationships in the data that people would not spot by hand.

earns.quote: to discover trends / patterns / to find relationships

strong.sentence: Data mining can improve sales and profits, because the business can target its advertising at the types of customer most likely to buy.

earns.quote: used to improve sales / profits (1st) by targeting customers / demographics (1)

strong.sentence: The information it extracts also gives managers a sound basis for their decisions, instead of guesswork.

earns.quote: provides a sound basis for decision-making

strong.sentence: On the other hand, the extracted information may not be accurate, because it depends on how good the source data set is.

earns.quote: extracted information may not be accurate (1st) depends on source of data set (1)

strong.sentence: The business must also protect the privacy of the individuals in the data and follow data protection laws, which adds work and risk.

earns.quote: must ensure privacy of individuals / conform to data protection regulations

weak.answer: A two-column table: Benefits | Drawbacks; trends | expensive; profit | privacy; decisions | storage.
weak.why: Single words in a table name points but give no reasons or effects. There is no discussion and no expansion mark.

basis.quote: Furthermore, if these answers are shown in a sketched table, they do not properly answer the question as there is no discussion.

thin_evidence: 80 parts. 77 have mark schemes, all from 2022 to 2025. The 3 parts from March 2026 have none. The 2025 mark schemes no longer print the bullet cap or the both-sides rule. For 2025, the advice on format comes from examiner reports.
